what_was_done.action: Implement coherence-outcome-classifier.ts — pure function classifyPendingEntries(journal, events, now) returning OutcomeAttribution[]
what_was_done.result: Per ADR-010: rule order is (1) negative within NEGATIVE_EVENT_HORIZON=5 epic-scoped events same-fingerprint, (2) positive on closure event, (3) positive after POSITIVE_TIME_HORIZON_MS=24h elapsed without re-escalation. Constants exported for tuning. Pure — only `import type` from coherence-journal and event-log; zero fs/net.

Builds rule via factory(opts) matching coherence-escalation.ts pattern. matches() reads CoherenceJournal.all() each tick, runs classifier, returns one ReconcilerMatch per attribution with idempotencyKey embedding entryId+outcome. act() calls journal.updateOutcome. Per-entry act error caught/logged; classifier filter on outcome!==pending blocks redundant disk traffic. Journal read failure short-circuits to empty matches.

what_was_done.result: All 24 pass. Boundary tests: 4-event/5-event/6-event for negative horizon; 23h/24h/25h for time horizon. Closure-after, closure-before, different-epic, negative-trumps-closure-rule-order, malformed timestamps, multi-entry attribution all covered.

what_was_done.action: Write 9 reconciler-rule integration tests against real CoherenceJournal repository (tmpdir-backed JSONL)
what_was_done.result: All 9 pass. Verifies: rule shape (matches/act + name); end-to-end positive-horizon attribution with real Reconciler; negative attribution from real stage-dispatched event in event log; closure attribution from bead-status-changed event; idempotency (no-op on second tick when outcome already attributed); per-entry act error doesn't abort loop; journal read failure handled gracefully; multi-entry tick produces one match per attribution.

what_was_tested: Standard implementation depth (per builder.md § 5c). 24 classifier tests use plain object fixtures matching real JournalEntry + PipelineEvent shapes — no mocks of the unit under test. 9 reconciler-rule tests use real CoherenceJournal repository (tmpdir-backed JSONL via fs.mkdtemp) wired into a real Reconciler instance with real event-log appends — true integration depth on the file boundary even though this bead is technically a 'standard' bead by the verification matrix (no service/API boundary, no transactional logic). Boundary cases named: 'BOUNDARY: re-escalation as 4th epic-scoped event → negative (within horizon)', 'BOUNDARY: re-escalation as 5th epic-scoped event → negative (at horizon)', 'BOUNDARY: re-escalation as 6th epic-scoped event → NOT negative (outside horizon)', 'BOUNDARY: 23h elapsed without re-escalation → still pending', 'BOUNDARY: exactly 24h elapsed without re-escalation → positive (horizon)'. Idempotency case: 'idempotency: classifier filters non-pending entries — second tick is a no-op'. Negative-trumps-closure: 'negative trumps closure when both apply (rule order)'. typecheck clean for both new files; ESLint clean for all four files. All four coherence-related test suites (this bead's two + the existing coherence-journal + coherence-escalation) run together: 69/69 pass with no regressions.
deviations_from_ac: AC #1 verified: classifyPendingEntries exported, pure (only `import type`). AC #2: OutcomeAttribution {entryId, outcome:'positive'|'negative', rationale} exported. AC #3: negative rule + tests; 'within 5 events' formalised as count of epic-scoped events whose timestamp > entry.timestamp AND <= candidate-event.timestamp, INCLUSIVE of candidate (5th event = at horizon, 6th = outside). AC #4: closure rule + tests; signal = bead-status-changed event with payload.beadId === entry.epicId AND payload.newStatus === 'closed'. AC #5: time-horizon rule + tests; uses now.getTime() - entryMs >= POSITIVE_TIME_HORIZON_MS. AC #6: NEGATIVE_EVENT_HORIZON=5 and POSITIVE_TIME_HORIZON_MS=24*60*60*1000 exported as module constants with ADR-010 inline references. AC #7: rule conforms to ReconcilerRule interface (name, matches, act); minTickIntervalMs supported. AC #8: rule reads via CoherenceJournal repository (factory pattern allows test-seam injection); persists via updateOutcome. AC #9: per-entry try/catch in act(); classifier filters non-pending entries. AC #10: 24 classifier tests cover all named scenarios + boundaries. AC #11: 9 rule tests against real tmpdir CoherenceJournal. AC #12: ADR-010 referenced in module header + on each constant. Tests placed at beads_web/__tests__/lib/coherence-outcome-classifier.test.ts and beads_web/__tests__/lib/reconciler-rules/coherence-outcome-attribution.test.ts so jest can discover them; AC #10 + #11 ('tests pass') would otherwise be unreachable. Production-code paths match the manifest exactly. Reviewer concurred that this is a manifest-typo correction, not a scope deviation.
surprises_or_findings: Closure-event signal contract: ADR-010 step 2 says 'Epic reaches status=closed' but the architecture deliberately leaves the SIGNAL open. Per the bead's CONTEXT THE AGENT NEEDS section ('determine by querying bd state or by reading reconciler-action-taken events. Architecture leaves this open — pick the simpler signal (event-based) and document'), I chose: a `bead-status-changed` event with payload.beadId === entry.epicId AND payload.newStatus === 'closed'. NO production code emits this event today (verified via repo grep for 'bead-status-changed'); the contract is forward-looking. Practical consequence: until a future bead emits the event (e.g., wrapping bd close, or as part of wlsr.9 retroactive rollout), the closure rule never fires and the time-horizon rule provides default-positive after 24h — exactly ADR-010's 'tolerance for wrong calls is high' default-positive stance. This choice is documented in the module header (lines 43-50 of coherence-outcome-classifier.ts) and the reviewer concurred. Re-escalation signal: stage-dispatched + payload.toAction === 'run-coherence-agent' (matches what coherence-escalation.ts and the post-wlsr.7 generalised rule already fire). Path deviation surfaced separately under deviations_from_ac (cosmetic; same as wlsr.2 had).
recommendation_for_next: wlsr.6 is fully integrated: when wlsr.7 lands its generalised escalation rule (Wave 2 sibling) and registers it, every stage-dispatched(run-coherence-agent) event will produce a re-escalation signal that this classifier consumes. Wave 3 cutover beads (wlsr.14/15/16) will exercise this end-to-end: rule.act() escalates → coherence dispatched → journal entry written → next-tick classifier eventually attributes positive (horizon, default) or negative (re-escalation within 5 events). To activate the closure rule sooner: a small follow-on bead can wire a `bead-status-changed` event emit into bd close (or into a beads_web lifecycle hook that watches bd state transitions) — purely additive; classifier already reads the contract. wlsr.9 (rollout script) can also consider initialising the journal directory with a lifecycle hook that emits bead-status-changed events for already-closed parked beads to attribute their pre-existing journal entries positive. Reconciler bootstrap: register this rule in src/lib/reconciler-bootstrap.ts (not done in this bead — out of scope; that wiring belongs to a separate integration bead or to wlsr.9). Until registered, the rule is exercised only by tests; no production effect.
